Meeting header:
  Date/Time: 2026-02-10 15:30 UTC
  Duration: ~52 minutes
  Location: Zoom

Transcript:
[00:00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have an hour blocked, so we'll try to keep this tight. I'm Avery, Redwood AE, Marcus and Lena from our solutions team are here.
[00:00:12] Rajiv: Hi all. Rajiv here — Head of Cloud Partnerships at VectorShift. Appreciate the time.
[00:00:18] Sofia: Sofia, Solutions Architect. I'll be owning the SSO/compliance side.
[00:00:23] Tom: Tom — Product. Focusing on the pilot workloads and how we present this on the marketplace listing.
[00:00:30] Marcus: Cool. Quick agenda: ref-arch options, packaging for marketplace (AMI/container + listing artifacts), pilot scope, security checklist, next steps. Anything to add?
[00:00:42] Rajiv: Sounds good. Also pricing alignment for the listing — not deep commercial discussion but rough units.
[00:00:47] Avery: We'll surface pricing guidance but won't finalize here. Ok Marcus, take it away on ref-arch.

[00:01:05] Marcus: Thanks. So we have two main deployment patterns to propose for the joint solution: 1) Redwood-hosted integration where VectorShift users can subscribe to a managed offering, and 2) a Marketplace 'bring-your-own-vpc' deployment where customers install a connector from the VectorShift marketplace listing which points to a customer-managed VPC or dedicated Redwood nodes. For the ref-arch doc we'll show both and call out tradeoffs: latency and compliance favors dedicated/private; time-to-value favors hosted.
[00:01:45] Sofia: Quick question on the 'connector' — is that a container image or an AMI?
[00:01:50] Marcus: Great question. For the marketplace packaging, we typically produce containerized deployment manifests (helm charts) plus a reference Terraform module. We can also provide an AMI if the marketplace requires it — we should map to VectorShift's marketplace packaging rules.
[00:02:10] Tom: Our marketplace supports both but prefers a container/Helm entry for managed clusters. We'll need a sample Helm chart and a lightweight operator.

[00:02:28] Lena: On networking: if we go BYOVPC we need to document VPC peering options, egress rules, and private link endpoints for telemetry. Also KV-cache and state transfer between nodes need proper security controls.
[00:02:46] Sofia: 'Private link' — do you mean a private endpoint or a managed private link? We need details because our security team will ask about cross-account access.
[00:02:55] Marcus: Yes, both options can be supported. We'll include diagrams for: VPC peering, PrivateLink, and a dedicated router model for cross-account calls.

[00:03:15] [Noise: 1s] Rajiv: On the compliance side, can you summarize what logs and audit trail you capture for private deployments vs hosted?
[00:03:23] Avery: Sure. For hosted: we have request-level logs, token usage, and per-route latency metrics retained per our plan; we can push audit exports to a customer S3/GCS with encryption. For private/dedicated: all logs can stay within the customer's account/VPC, and we support KMS envelope encryption with customer-managed keys.
[00:03:45] Sofia: Do you support HSM-based keys or only KMS? Our customers sometimes require an HSM-backed KMS.
[00:03:52] Marcus: We support KMS and integrations with HSM-backed solutions — but the onboarding window increases a bit because of key handoff and attestation. We'll document the process.

[00:04:12] Tom: For the pilot we want low friction: can we start with a dedicated sandbox in Redwood, then move to BYOVPC for customers who need it?
[00:04:21] Avery: That's our recommended approach — Redwood Dedicated for pilot throughput+observability, then we help transition to BYOVPC if a customer requires isolation.

[00:04:35] Rajiv: On success metrics — we propose: 99th percentile latency under 300ms for the small text-gen workload, cost per 1k tokens under $0.XX (TBD), and a reproducible benchmark that we can publish on the listing.
[00:04:52] Marcus: We'll need Tom's sample prompts and expected completion sizes to run realistic benchmarks.
[00:04:58] Tom: I'll share three workloads: short-generation chat, long-form summarization, and an embeddings pipeline for search re-rank.

[00:05:12] [00:05:12] Sofia: I also need to validate data residency: some EMEA customers want EU-only hosting. Is that an option for hosted or just private?
[00:05:22] Marcus: We have EU regions available in Redwood Hosted; for stricter controls customers usually prefer private deployments inside their own VPC or an on-prem bundle. We'll list region options in the ref-arch.

[00:05:42] Rajiv: Marketplace listing assets — what exactly do you need from us?
[00:05:48] Avery: From VectorShift: a short product description, logos (SVG), sample screenshots or demo link, support contact, three use-cases, compliance artifacts you'd like referenced. From us: deployment manifests, an integration guide, performance notes, and a co-branded architecture diagram. We'll produce a checklist and a draft listing page.
[00:06:12] Tom: About the demo: we want an embedded live demo in the listing or at least a video. Do you have a reference way to bootstrap that?
[00:06:19] Lena: We can provide a short 2–3 minute sandbox demo that runs in a secure iframe or links to a disposable sandbox. We'll include sample keys and rate limits for the demo mode.

[00:06:36] Marcus: On packaging: expected artifacts are helm chart + values, terraform module, sample IAM policies, ref-arch diagram (PNG + svg), security checklist, and a 'how-to' quickstart. We'll attach all to the marketplace listing.

[00:06:52] Sofia: For the security checklist, our compliance folks will ask for SOC2/ISO status docs, pen test reports, and a data flow map. Can you share SOC2 attestation?
[00:07:02] Avery: Yes, we'll share latest SOC2 report under NDA and a redacted pen test summary. We'll also include our data flow diagrams.

[00:07:12] Rajiv: Good. Now operationally — who owns support for a listing customer? If someone purchases through VectorShift marketplace, does VectorShift handle first-line support or is Redwood the primary?
[00:07:24] Tom: We prefer joint support: VectorShift handles onboarding and billing, Redwood handles runtime incidents and SLAs. We can define an escalation matrix in the listing documentation.

[00:07:36] Marcus: Agree. We'll put an on-call contact and runbook in the marketplace docs.

[00:07:44] [00:07:44] Sofia: A slightly technical question: does Redwood create a per-tenant KV cache or a shared cache? We care about noisy neighbor isolation.
[00:07:53] Marcus: The runtime supports both. For multi-tenant hosted deployments we use namespace isolation and per-tenant cache partitions. For dedicated deployments, it's isolated by node group. We'll call this out and include recommended cache TTL and sizing guidance.

[00:08:10] Rajiv: About billing metrics for the marketplace — do you expose token-level billing or only aggregate invoices?
[00:08:17] Avery: We expose token-level breakdowns per account and per-route; for marketplace integration we can map those to VectorShift's customer IDs via a connector so you get pass-through usage.

[00:08:27] Tom: On the PoC timeline you mentioned 3 weeks — can you outline high-level milestones?
[00:08:33] Marcus: Week 0: infra provisioning and access. Week 1: deploy and run smoke tests, basic functional validation. Week 2: run benchmarks and collect metrics, integrate logging exports. Week 3: iterate on performance/latency and finalize listing artifacts.

[00:08:52] Sofia: Do we need legal pre-approval for the joint listing? Some marketplaces require a legal review.
[00:08:58] Avery: We'll surface a minimal legal checklist: trademarks, logos, data processing addendum. We can work with your legal team.

[00:09:12] [Short pause] Rajiv: A practical item — our security team asked about network egress controls. If a customer uses hosted integration, can we guarantee no outbound telemetry to third-party endpoints except as documented?
[00:09:26] Marcus: Yes. We can document exactly which endpoints are used for telemetry, and provide an allowlist. For private deployments telemetry stays in the customer's network unless they opt-in to sending to Redwood for managed monitoring.

[00:09:40] Tom: Are there any blockers you foresee for doing the initial sandbox pilot?
[00:09:44] Marcus: The main blockers: IAM access for provisioner, KMS key exchange if using CMKs, and getting the sample prompt set for benchmarks. Otherwise it's a straightforward deploy.

[00:09:56] Sofia: About SSO — we use SAML primarily, but OIDC in some customers. Do you have examples for both?
[00:10:03] Lena: We support SAML and OIDC. We'll include metadata examples and a short SSO setup guide.

[00:10:12] Rajiv: Ok let's talk deliverables and owners to close this out.
[00:10:18] Avery: Action items: I'll circulate the draft ref-arch and marketplace checklist by next Tuesday. Marcus will build the pilot runbook. Sofia will share SSO metadata. Tom will send sample workloads. Rajiv — if you can confirm which marketplace listing type (container vs AMI) by end of week that helps.

[00:10:36] Rajiv: Confirmed — we'll aim for container/Helm listing.

[00:10:40] Marcus: Also nominated timeline: infra provisioning target week of Feb 23. We'll send DDL for test accounts.

[00:10:50] [00:10:50] Sofia: Quick nit: in the ref-arch, please call out fallback policies and circuit breakers for the model endpoint — customers want data safety and predictable degraded behavior.
[00:11:00] Marcus: Yes, we'll include fallback model variants, throttling rules, and a canary rollout snippet for helm.

[00:11:12] Tom: For the marketplace blurb, we need a short value prop of 2 sentences and 3 bullet benefits. We'll draft and share.

[00:11:22] Avery: Great. Anything else?
[00:11:26] Rajiv: One last thing: any benchmarking scripts or harness you use?
[00:11:30] Marcus: We use a lightweight harness that hits endpoints with configurable seq length and concurrency; we'll open-source the harness snippet and share a small sample dataset. Expect that in the runbook.

[00:11:42] [Background: brief keyboard] Sofia: Noted. We'll wait for the doc links.\n[00:11:48] Avery: I'll close and recap. Next steps are captured in the action items. We'll follow up with a calendar invite for pilot kickoff once infra is ready. Thanks everyone.

[00:11:58] Tom: Thanks folks.
[00:12:00] Rajiv: Thanks.
